comment: Hello and thank you for allowing me to once again express my support for the Triple Crown event. In the past, I have supported the event from a business perspective. Now, I want to also share the great times my kids had going to the games and watching these talented young athletes. I felt comfortable allowing my kids to attend in my absence. It gave them both motivation to practice and play harder at the sports they were both involved in as they could see that college scouts were also in attendance. This is one of the few events that a parent can check all the boxes; free, safe, healthy fun and no alcohol permitted. Please consider renewing the contract for Triple Crown. We need the diversity in our town that is becoming more and more like a town for the very elite.

comment: I am aware you have heard from me numerous times, on behalf of the Park City Soccer Club and our Extreme Cup Soccer Tournament. In lieu of repeating myself this evening during the City Council's discussion about Triple Crown Sports and their desire for a new City Services Agreement, I will submit this brief statement so PCSC is on the record in response to Council's request for community input. Park City Soccer Club (PCSC) believes in the importance of youth-based events, the experiences they provide, and the benefits they bring to the community (all of which Council has heard before.) For this reason, our organization does not object to the Triple Crown Tournaments returning to Park City each summer. Our concerns on the subject, however, are two-fold: 1. We are opposed to the concept of overlapping Extreme Cup and Triple Crown dates, and the need to share field space. The negative economic impact is a burden on PCSC and our social equity based scholarship program, while the logistics are difficult for all parties including City staff. 2. We remain surprised, and honestly frustrated, by the level of in-kind support afforded to TCS through Fee Waivers, We are aware the discussion at hand is about TCS, not Park City Soccer Club, however it is difficult to understand how a for-profit, out-of-state business can be granted tens of thousands of dollars in subsidies while a local non, profit -- dedicated to supporting Park City's own underserved population through event proceeds -- continues to receive less than $2,000 in fee waivers / event subsidies each year. (Our 2021 City Fee Waivers totaled $1,725.) We have spoken at length with Jenny Diersen, and believe staff has done a good job of presenting workable options for moving forward. It is our hope that Council's consideration will focus on elements of Options 2 or 3, as opposed to TCS's proposal.
